article.Citation/Title: Savage, C., & McCabe, O. L. (1973). Residential psychedelic (LSD) therapy for the narcotic addict: A controlled study. Archives of General Psychiatry, 28(6), 808-814.
article.Outcome: 25% vs 5% (9/36 vs 2/37) verified abstinent at 12-month follow-up
article.InterventionDescription: Single high-dose LSD session (300-450µg) after ~24 hours preparatory psychotherapy over 4-6 weeks residential halfway-house stay; one week post-session integration therapy.

ae_events.Description: One treatment-group patient died of aortic stenosis ~5 months post-treatment, before completing 12-month follow-up; not attributed to LSD.
In-session fear, mistrust and self-reported panic/abreaction during the LSD experience in one illustrative case (Theodore), managed by therapist support, no rescue medication.
Transient nausea during LSD dosing session in one illustrative case (Theodore); patient described stomach discomfort tied to anxiety.

article.Outcome: Results, first paragraph: 'nine (25%) of the 36 subjects in the treatment group maintained total abstinence from narcotic drugs for at least one year as opposed to two (5%) of 37 in the control group (P<.05; see Table 3).' This is the article's headline, abstract-led outcome ('Comparative verified abstinence data throughout the first posttreatment year were significantly in favor of the treatment group.'). Chose the strict-abstinence dichotomy over the article's secondary recomputation that includes briefly-relapsed patients (12/37 = 33.3%), since the strict figure is the one carried into Table 3's chi-square test and is not itself a subgroup redefinition.
article.SD: Table 3 (x2 Analysis of Differences in Abstinence...) is badly OCR-garbled: the (0-6 mo) row prints 5 bare numbers (12, 25, 34, 5.35, .03), the (7-12 mo) row prints 6 (13, 3, 23, 33, 6.51, .02), and the (0-12 mo) row prints only 4 (27, 34, 3.86, .05), with no consistent column structure and no row reconciling to the stated N=36/37 or 9/2 counts. Per the anti-fabrication rule, declined to guess which figure (e.g. the isolated 3.86) is the chi-square paired with the 12-month abstinence result rather than inventing a decoding rule; coded '.' and flagging the table as unusable in its current OCR state.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 36 treatment-group subjects (37 originally, minus 1 who died of aortic stenosis before the 12-month point and was therefore excluded from the 12-month abstinence analysis) + 37 control-group subjects = 73, the denominator underlying the 9/36 vs 2/37 comparison in Outcome.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 11/14 met. No sample-size or power justification anywhere. Blinding is never mentioned in either direction (not implemented and not stated as absent), so it does not meet the 'described, including as absent' bar. No dedicated harms/safety assessment or section is described (harms information that does exist is incidental, in Results and the case illustrations, not a described methodology element). Funding is disclosed (grant MH-15555, Friends Medical Science Research Center) with no explicit COI statement, which is sufficient per the field rule for funding_coi=Y.

article.Retention (%): 78 volunteers were randomly assigned; 74 comprised the final study sample (the abstract states '37 completers in each group'), because 4 subjects originally assigned to the treatment condition transferred to the regular program before receiving LSD and were excluded from analysis. 74/78 x 100 = 94.9%, using randomized N (78) as denominator per the rule (both randomized and enrolled/completer counts are reported).
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Table 1 reports only one non-white race category, 'Black (%)' = 76 for the total sample (78% treatment, 73% control); no other non-white groups are reported, so no summation was needed.
article.PercentFem: Explicitly 'All male narcotic addicts in Maryland correctional institutions' were eligible/enrolled; coded 0 as an explicitly reported fact, not a missing value.
article.MediatingYN: A 'psychedelic experience questionnaire' identified 'peak reactors' (29/36, 80%) and the article compares their adjustment scores to the whole treatment group descriptively (mean 4.7, identical to the group as a whole), with no indirect-effect test, regression-based mediation model, or formal statistical test of the peak experience as a mechanism linking LSD to abstinence. This is a narrative/descriptive subgroup comparison, so MediatingYN = 0, not 1, per the field's rule.
article.ModeratingYN: No treatment-by-moderator interaction test was run; the peak-experience analysis compares adjustment ratings only within the treatment arm (peak vs non-peak reactors), not as an interaction with treatment assignment. No formal moderation analysis was conducted, so ModeratingYN = 0.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: MMPI and IQ tests (Raven, Otis) are validated instruments but are reported only as baseline characterization within the two individual case illustrations (Theodore W., Wally B.), not as a trial-level outcome compared between treatment and control. The trial's actual outcomes are urine-verified abstinence (not a scale) and an unpublished, non-validated 'Global Adjustment Rating Scale' (McCabe and Shock, unpublished data, 1972). Coded 0.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Sample is restricted to volunteer parolees aged 21-50 with >=18 months remaining before parole, medically/psychologically screened (excluding organic brain damage, active liver disease, cardiovascular disease, florid psychosis), and self-selected under an acknowledged prison-coercion caveat ('it is questionable that anyone in prison can be considered a true volunteer'; candidates were shown a film emphasizing LSD's dangers before consenting). Coded 0 as a highly screened, volunteer, incarcerated sample rather than an unselected real-world clinical population.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Table 1 reports 54% unskilled laborers and mean 8.6 years education for the sample; the clinic is described as being 'on the fringe of the Baltimore ghetto area.' No explicit income/public-insurance criterion is given, but occupational, educational, and setting descriptors substantively describe a low-SES population; coded 1 as a judgment call.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: MMPI is administered and referenced only within the two individual case illustrations (Theodore W., Wally B.), not analyzed or reported as a treatment-vs-control group outcome anywhere in Results; coded 0.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: The 'Global Adjustment Rating Scale' assesses residential, occupational, and interpersonal functioning tied to parole/rehabilitation status (Fig 2), which is treated here as a rehabilitation/adjustment outcome distinct from a formal quality-of-life instrument; coded 0 as a judgment call.
article.CulturalFraming: Comment section explicitly names the racial dynamic as a study limitation: 'a wide sociocultural gulf existed between the white therapist and the predominantly black patient group. Black therapists could be expected to have a less difficult time establishing with the patients a relationship of trust, a crucial determinant of positive therapeutic outcome.' Table 1 also reports % Black by group. Coded 1.
article.BlindingYN: No blinding procedure of any kind (patient, therapist, or outcome rater) is described in Methods; the independent evaluation team rated adjustment from parole-agent interviews with no stated blinding to group assignment. Coded 0 as an absent, undescribed design element (this is why 'blinding' = N rather than Y in MethodologyDescribedYN: the absence itself was never stated by the authors, only inferable from silence).
article.MortalityMeasured: One treatment-group death (aortic stenosis, unrelated to LSD per the authors) is reported in Results as an incidental fact affecting the 12-month abstinence denominator, not as a designed mortality endpoint. Per the field rule, a death reported anywhere counts as MortalityMeasured=1 and generates an ae_events row (AE01), even though causally unrelated to the intervention.
article.SafetyReported: Borderline call. There is no dedicated Adverse Events/Safety section or table. However the article does report specific, patient-level safety-relevant events: the treatment-group death (with cause given), and case-illustration content describing in-session fear/mistrust/panic and nausea, plus an authors' summary sentence that 'the partial regression and loosening of defenses during the LSD experience tend to precipitate panic, somatic complaints, and abreaction' in patients like Theodore. Coded 'Y' (safety-relevant information is genuinely reported, even if informally and not systematically across the full N) rather than 'N', per the cardinal rule against understating harm reporting when real signal is present in the text.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Three distinct types identified from the text: (1) death/aortic stenosis, (2) in-session fear/panic/abreaction (challenging-experience phenomenology), (3) transient nausea. Types (2) and (3) are illustrated via a single named case (Theodore) rather than counted across the cohort, so this is a much softer count than a systematic AE table; flagged here rather than defaulted to 'Not numbered' because the three qualitatively distinct event types are each clearly nameable even though their per-type N is not.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: No statement anywhere gives a count of how many of the 36-41 treatment-group patients experienced fear/panic, nausea, or any other adverse effect; only the death has a stated N (1). Coded '.' for the article as a whole.
article.AE_denominator: No explicit statement of a safety-assessed population size; the panic/nausea events are drawn from one illustrative case narrative, not a systematically monitored-N cohort. Coded 'Not numbered' rather than '.' because some safety information was in fact reported (SafetyReported=Y).
article.WorstSeverity: Driven entirely by AE01 (death = CTCAE grade 5 / FDA seriousness criterion = Severe per rubric). This is flagged explicitly because the authors themselves attribute the death to a pre-existing, unrelated cardiac condition (aortic stenosis), not to LSD or the study intervention; WorstSeverity nonetheless reflects the mortality-reporting rule rather than any causal judgment about the intervention's safety.
article.SchemaRevisionNote: 2026-09-03 schema-revision splice: ConfoundYN/PVal removed, MediatingYN/ModeratingYN/HypothesisTestReportedYN added, sourced from a separate v3 extraction run (PromptVersion v1.3) rather than this file's own v1.2 run. Every other field in this file is unchanged from the original v1.2 extraction -- this file is now a hybrid of two runs for these 3 fields only. See clinical_adjudication.md '2026-09-03 -- Coding-scheme revision' for the full rationale.

ae_events.Savage 1973_AE01: Results section: 'One of the original 37 patients in the treatment group died before reaching the 12 months follow-up point; he had maintained five posttreatment months of complete abstinence before dying of aortic stenosis.' Onset coded 'delayed' because death occurred post-discharge, well beyond the acute dosing period (~5 months out). Severity graded Severe per rubric (death = Grade 5) using SeveritySource='rubric' because the authors report the fact and cause of death but assign no CTCAE grade or SAE label and use no severity language of their own; this is a pre-1980 article and the 'author' source was not used because no author severity language exists for this event.
ae_events.Savage 1973_AE02: Drawn from the Theodore W. case illustration: his own session-report quote ('I was making myself afraid by self-imposed mistrust... I was looking for a demon to jump out at me any moment') and the authors' following summary ('the partial regression and loosening of defenses during the LSD experience tend to precipitate panic, somatic complaints, and abreaction'). Graded Mild per the rubric's default for expected, in-session, non-pharmacologically-managed challenging-experience phenomenology (the patient was reassured/held the therapist's hand, no rescue medication, remained in and completed the session). SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because it is unclear from a single illustrative case how many of the cohort this generalizes to, and whether severity varied for other patients the authors' summary sentence may be describing collectively rather than just Theodore.
ae_events.Savage 1973_AE03: Also from Theodore W.'s quoted session report: 'My stomach began to feel nauseated somewhat and I put emphasis on this rather than something of importance.' Treated as a distinct physical symptom (AE_type='AE') separate from the psychological fear/panic content (AE02). Graded Mild as a transient, expected, self-limiting acute drug effect with no intervention described; SeverityIndeterminate='N' since the description, though from one case, is specific enough to grade confidently.

config_proposal.note: Primary outcome is a 2x2 verified-abstinence comparison at 12 months (25% vs 5%, P<.05); converting proportions to an odds ratio is a defensible but assumption-carrying step (a methodologist would want to see it), and Table 3's chi-square figures are OCR-garbled and could not be used to corroborate a chi2-based conversion instead, so this is proposed as 'approx' rather than 'clean'.
